text:
maria: Quick check — I'm prepping the per-customer feature-flag rollout for the new dedupe logic. Need agreement on gating: contract-level allowlist + opt-in for VIPs + a 1% canary for new enterprise customers. any objections?
josh: sounds fine. What's the exact behavior when a customer is not on the allowlist but contract mentions the feature? do we block or soft-fail?
neil: prefer blocking by default unless there's explicit opt-in in the contract. Otherwise we risk surprise usage and billing diff.
maria: ok default=blocked. we expose a `contract_gated` flag that the billing sync flips during invoice processing if contract has feature. also need a runtime fallback for dev/test accounts.
sophia: +1. runtime fallback should return 403-like structured error so clients can surface a clear message, not a silent degrade. e.g. {"error": "feature_not_enabled_for_account"} or a short human message.
josh: re: VIPs — we have a handful of pilot customers that should be allowed even if contract flag isn't set yet. propose allowlist keyed by account id and a label `pilot=true`. ops can toggle via the console or CLI.
maria: agreed. I'll add an allowlist table with columns: account_id, reason, expires_at, actor. will wire console to edit.
neil: canary plan: start at 1% of eligible enterprise accounts (random stable hash on account id) for 48h -> 5% for a week -> open. Have rollback metric triggers for error rate > 0.5% or latency tail shift.
sophia: add a quality guard: run golden prompts evals on every rollout step to detect output regressions. tie to regression-alerts in Optimize.
josh: operational question: who has permission to flip allowlist entries? I'd like to limit to SRE + Customer Success. also record audit log.
maria: ops perms = @sre, @cs, and a special "flag-admin" role. changes create an audit event with actor and ip. console will show last modified.
deploy-bot: deploy started: featureflag-service v3.4.1 -> canary cluster (tag: contract-gate).
neil: note for implementers: kernel path changes might affect latency for large contexts. make sure batching policies keep CPU steady for allowlist path. If fallback path hits often, we should gate batching config.
maria: good call. i'll add a tiny feature flag `ff_enable_fastpath` that is enabled for host-level deployments only; disabled in private deployments by default.
sophia: code review ping @josh @neil — PR #512 implements the runtime check and error payload. please review by EOD.
josh: looking now. quick: ensure the SDK surface exposes a typed error class so clients can do `if (err.code === 'FEATURE_NOT_ENABLED')` rather than parsing strings.
maria: yes will return `code=FEATURE_NOT_ENABLED`, `feature=dedupe_v2`, `docs_url` in payload.
neil: test matrix: unit tests for contract flag true/false, allowlist present/absent, canary hashing deterministic, and integration test hitting the console toggle. also add a load test with 10k reqs/s to verify no hotpath regress.
sophia: can we have a query in console that shows "accounts affected by contract mismatch" so sales can proactively reach out?
josh: yep we can surface pending-contract-flag accounts. that's part of the rollout dashboard.
maria: action items: 1) josh/neil review PR #512 (EOD) 2) maria wire console allowlist UI (tomorrow) 3) sophia hookup evals -> optimize (wednesday) 4) ops to confirm role mapping + audit (tomorrow) 5) deploy canary tonight 00:30 UTC. I'll post a follow-up thread with the exact rollout times. anyone else? :eyes:
josh: canary healthcheck query? share the prometheus query and i'll add to dashboard.
neil: i'll post the query in the PR comments.
maria: thanks all — ping me if you need owner handoff during deploy. :thumbsup:
